curriculum: The programme-specific 2026–2027 regulations confirm the full-time Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. The example preserves the fully Dutch-taught subject-specific track: 127.5 EC major plus 52.5 EC profiling. The major combines two 30 EC base packages, a 30 EC depth package, two shared advanced courses totaling 15 EC, a 7.5 EC methods choice, a 7.5 EC corpus course and a 7.5 EC thesis in Dutch. The level-3 depth package and shared advanced courses provide 45 EC even before the corpus course and thesis, satisfying the advanced major floor. The profiling allocation includes a 30 EC coherent package. Crossing Borders is separately formal, has a 135 EC major and may teach up to one third in English. The first-listed language package and methods option are retained independently of UCR fit.
progression: The regulations distinguish the 2026–27 intake from transitional curricula and prescribe a compulsory zero-credit basic grammar test. The student guide positions two base packages before the depth package and identifies writing development across the degree. The corpus course is offered in block 2 or 3 and prepares the supervised 7.5 EC final thesis in Dutch. The thesis follows this preparation and may be scheduled in any block subject to registration. Electives include a coherent 30 EC package chosen from the approved options, with prior permission for external or international selections. The reviewed comparison shows the curriculum rather than certifying an individual timetable.
